_comment: Every external input this project depends on, with where to get it and what
it must hash to. This file is committed; the artefacts are not.
Rule: a source is not usable until its hash is recorded here. `tools/fetch-sources.sh`
refuses to report success on a file whose hash does not match, and refuses to
silently skip one it could not fetch.
base        the primary source tree the build is derived from
reference   read and cross-checked against, never built from
baseline    the upstream RE project, pinned, read-only, supplies the differential
now         needed before R0/R2 can start
later       needed at the gate named in `needed_by`
manual      cannot be scripted; a human obtains it

pin.subject: A guard case that expired on the day the thing it guards started working

upstream.why: The differential proof in R9 is only credible if the baseline it compares against is one this project cannot edit. The commit hash IS that proof.
supplies: test-cases.toml (58 registered tests with pre-written refutation conditions)
reports/*.json (74 measured reports across three builds)
docs/disclosure.md (which findings are held and why)
tools/ (loader-tftp, mkramboot, console-lint, console-dump, loader-unpack, mkflash, rtcase, the CI checkers)

source_trees.why: The only public drop whose target board IS an RTL8196E (ALFA AIP-W512). Carries linux-2.6.30, busybox-1.13, users/, romfs/, boards/rtl8196eu/, and BOTH rsdk toolchains.
source_trees.matches_device: gcc 4.4.5-1.5.5p2 / uClibc 0.9.30.3 / Linux 2.6.30.9 — every field of the device's own kernel banner. HYPOTHESIS until R2a measures it.
source_trees.caveat: ALFA's board, not TOTOLINK's. DDR timing, PHY config and GPIO pin assignment may all differ, and getting them wrong does not necessarily crash.

source_trees.why: The only public source for the rtl819x BOOTLOADER (rtl819x/bootcode/). Needed to read what the loader does, and for R10c if a first-stage loader is ever attempted.
source_trees.caveat: A different bootcode generation from this unit's 2014.04.22 v1.3. Do not assume the command set matches — the device's own `?` output (upstream notes/uart-pinout.md) is authoritative.

source_trees.why: rtl819x/users/boa/apmib/apmib.{c,h} — the MIB table the device's libapmib.so is a build of. Upstream already used it to give the recovered MIB table an outside witness (SUPER_NAME=180, USER_NAME=182).
source_trees.needed_by: R2b, R7b (config store schema), D8 (CVE-2024-21778 TLV parser)

source_trees.why: Realtek's own OpenWrt SDK. Carries arch/rlx (the Lexra kernel architecture port), drivers/net/rtl819x/ (rtl865x_*), drivers/net/wireless/rtl8192cd/.
source_trees.caveat: ODM-quality code. Read it as a description of what the hardware needs, never as a model of how to write a driver.

source_trees.why: A SECOND independent implementation of the rtl819x network driver (target/linux/realtek/files/drivers/net/rtl819x/, incl. rtl_nic.c). Two implementations of the same hardware is what makes a register reading a measurement instead of a transcription.
SDK v3.4.9.3 on Linux 3.10 — the K2 candidate, i.e. the first kernel generation where MIPS has device tree.
source_trees.caveat: Its documented targets are RTL8198C/8814/8194. Whether RTL8196E is supported is UNVERIFIED.

source_trees.why: The furthest anyone has publicly taken RTL8196E on a modern kernel: OpenWrt master + Linux 4.14, arch/rlx, with GPIO/PCI/IRQ/timers working. K3 reference.
source_trees.caveat: 'Working' is a forum claim, not a measurement. Switch driver incomplete, WiFi not started.

source_trees.why: The `files` branch carries the vendor datasheets. This is where refs/*.pdf come from.

A modern-kernel RTL8196E port carrying arch/mips/boot/dts/realtek/{rtl8196e.dtsi, rtl8196e_totolink_n100re.dts} -- a device tree for a TOTOLINK board on this SoC -- plus CPU_RLX4181 in cpu_type_enum, -march=rlx4181, R3000 cache paths, wait-instruction support, rdhwr emulation and a defconfig. It is the closest prior art to R5's drivers and DT bindings and to R10a/R10b.
source_trees.consumed_as: SECOND IMPLEMENTATION, NOT AN ANSWER. D12 source class 5: same SoC, so stronger than a sister-core document; written by someone who was also guessing, so weaker than a vendor SDK. One vote. Its use is to generate advance predictions and to fill the comparison column of docs/driver-diff.md -- R5 writes its drivers blind first, then diffs.
source_trees.caveat: Completeness is claimed by its author and its README, not established here. The first thing to do with it is read rtl8196e.dtsi's compatible strings and register addresses and check them against SPEC.md section 9 -- values already read on this unit. If they disagree, this tree may not be describing this part.

documents.handling: CITE, DO NOT COMMIT. See plan/router-rebuild-plan.md D12.

supplies.timer_watchdog: base 0xB800_3100 — TC0DATA 3100, TC1DATA 3104, TC0CNT 3108, TC1CNT 310C, TCCNR 3110, TCIR 3114, CDBR 3118, WDT 311C (sec 8.2)
supplies.spi_flash: controller with memory-mapped read, serial + dual I/O, up to 96.875 MHz (sec 7.3/7.4)
supplies.switch_core: base 0xBB80_4000 — Global Port Control 4000, MDC/MDIO Command 4004, MDC/MDIO Status 4008 (sec 11.1); LED control + topology + SCAN mode (sec 11.3)
supplies.pcie: host mode base 0xB8B0_1000 (sec 10.3) — NOTE: 0xB8B0 is PCIe, NOT the network MAC
supplies.pinmux: sec 6.1 Configuration upon Power-On Strapping, sec 6.2 Shared I/O Pin Mapping
supplies.ejtag: standard 5-signal P1149.1 test port (sec 1); DC params sec 13.10; boundary scan sec 14.2.4
supplies.cpu_claim: 'Embedded RISC CPU, RLX4181 with 16KB I-Cache, 8KB D-Cache, 16KB I-MEM, 8KB D-MEM' / 'Supports MIPS-1 ISA, MIPS16 ISA' / 'Clock Rate: 400MHz'
supplies.absent: no crypto / security engine section anywhere in the table of contents

caveats: It is a DRAFT. Draft and production silicon can differ.
It is the -VE1/2/3 variant, which has embedded DRAM by MCM. THIS UNIT HAS EXTERNAL SDRAM (Winbond W9825G6KH) and is therefore NOT this part.
Its CPU claim (RLX4181, MIPS-1) contradicts the common 'RTL8196E = RLX5281' convention AND the 142 lwl/lwr/swl/swr instructions in this device's own /bin/boa. See plan F34 and gate R1.
Therefore: no register value goes into code on this document's authority alone. Two independent sources, always (D12).

documents.kind_of_document: SCANNED IMAGES (11 CCITTFaxDecode streams, no text layer). Machine text extraction fails and correctly reports failure. A human reads it.
documents.why: The sibling part. Its CPU/Features bullet on the first pages is a FOURTH independent source for F34: if it also says RLX4181, the 'C=4181 / E=5281' convention is wrong in both directions and the R1 measurement is the only thing left standing.
documents.task: plan/DAY-ZERO.md item 6 — read one bullet with your eyes, ten seconds.

reference_only._comment: Read, cited, never downloaded. Listed so a claim in the plan can be traced to where it came from.

cve_and_advisories.about: rtl819x Jungle SDK config-file mib_init_value_array heap overflow — TLV length from the .dat file goes straight into memcpy. Drives D8's bounded TLV reader.
boa formWsc localPin OS command injection. Same defect site as CVE-2025-3987; two CVE families for one bug.

cve_and_advisories.id: Talos roundup, 15 vulns in this SDK
cve_and_advisories.about: The set upstream's prior-art.md refers to as 'Talos's fifteen reports on this SDK'.
Arbitrary firmware update on boa formUpload, CWE-347. The image-validation half of upstream D-12 is NOT original because of this.

platform.about: ggbruno's RTL8196E/97D/97F port to OpenWrt master + Linux 4.14. What works, what does not.
The long Realtek SoC support thread. Contains the EJTAG/Lexra notes: tjtag v3.0.1 and UrJTAG needed device IDs added; eJTAG pins muxed with EPHY_LED on some parts.
RFC: rtl8196 status — historical statement that mainline has no lexra support.
RFC v2: MIPS Lexra LX5280 CPU + Realtek RTL8186 SoC support. The mainline attempt.
Lexra history — cores execute virtually all MIPS instructions EXCEPT unaligned loads and stores. The patent story behind F34.
CONFIG_OF_FLATTREE landed in 2.6.34; MIPS device tree in 2.6.37. Source for F20.
Published spec: RTL8196C + 2 MB flash + 16 MB RAM. WRONG for this unit on all three counts — which is why a second-hand spare may genuinely be a different board.

binutils-2.24 Lexra patch. Adds six cores (lx4180, rlx4181, rlx4281, rlx5181, lx5280, rlx5281), all ISA_MIPS1; instruction masks INSN_4180=0x20000000 .. INSN_5281=0x00000040 and the RLXA/RLXB/RAD1/RAD2 groupings; 100+ Lexra-proprietary mnemonics (mta2/mfa/diva/multa/madda/msuba, lt/ltp/lwp/lhp/lbp/stp/swp, addr/subr/min/max/absr/cls/mux2, cmveqz/cmvnez, mtru/mfru/mtrk/mfrk, mflxc0/mtlxc0). Source of R1a's named Lexra ASE row (F52). NOTE: it does NOT disable lwl/lwr/swl/swr -- the assembler still accepts them. WHEN THIS IS FIRST DOWNLOADED (R2c) IT MOVES TO documents WITH A sha256.

gcc-4.8.4 Lexra patch. Maps TUNE_RLX onto TUNE_MIPS3000 (R3000 scheduling); disables lwl/lwr/swl/swr generation for Lexra targets via !TARGET_LEXRA && !TARGET_RLX on those patterns; adds -mno-bdsl (flag_fix_bdsl) forbidding loads in BRANCH delay slots -- which is NOT the load-use delay of F46, a distinction the plan must keep; gates conditional move on INSN_RLXB, which is what lets CPU-17's 18 movz/movn rule out baseline LX4180. Supplies -march=rlx5281 for D1's toolchain T-B. WHEN THIS IS FIRST DOWNLOADED (R2c) IT MOVES TO documents WITH A sha256.
Second RTL8196E Linux port; see source_trees/shibajee-linux-rtl8196e. Listed here too because it is cited in the plan before it is cloned.

A PUBLIC, redistributable RTL8196E-CG datasheet mirrored by a distributor -- not the leaked -VEx draft in refs/. Names the core RLX4181. Its value is that it can be linked from a public README where the leaked draft cannot, and that it is a second document (not the same one) on the naming question. It does not settle CPU-04: the device still says neither, and only PRId does.
